name: Dresden-II (NCC-1701)
summary: The NCC-1701 experiment placed an ultra-low-noise germanium detector near the Dresden-II reactor to search for very small nuclear recoils. It reported suggestive evidence for reactor CEvNS, with an interpretation strongly dependent on germanium quenching and background treatment.
detection_principle: A p-type point-contact germanium detector measures ionization from recoil interactions. Low electronic noise enables a sub-keV threshold. Reactor-on and reactor-off spectra are fitted with background and recoil-response models.
